text:
mike_sales: Customer asking how to wire logs/traces from Redwood POC into their Datadog/ELK. Seeing missing trace IDs in logs and 429s when sending embedding requests. Can eng ops help? CC @sara_se @danielle_se

sara_se: Can you drop sample logs and the request headers? Are they using our hosted API or dedicated?

mike_sales: Hosted. Sample log:
```
2026-03-18T15:12:01.123Z INFO [redwood-runtime] request completed status=200 model=gpt-large tokens=134 cost_usd=0.013
```
No request_id or trace headers.

danielle_se: We add X-Request-ID header on our SDKs; customers should forward it. For traces we set `x-redwood-trace` when available. If they're shipping via filebeat -> logstash -> elastic, they need to forward structured JSON with headers so Logstash can pick them up.

customer_xyz: We've set up filebeat -> logstash -> elastic. Logs show tokens but no trace id. Also got 429s in the POC when we hit batching endpoints.

observability_engineer: 429s are usually per-account burst limits on hosted. Check response headers like `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset`. For trace IDs, hosted emits the header but only if the request includes `X-Request-ID` or when tracing is sampled. Can you paste the raw HTTP request from the client?

customer_xyz: Here's the request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/responses
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, Content-Type: application/json
Body: { ... input: \"...\" }
```
No X-Request-ID header set by our app.

ops_bot: deploy: svc/poc-connector v1.2 rolled out to staging :rocket:

sara_se: Action items:
1) customer to add `X-Request-ID` per request (UUID). Redwood will mirror that to logs as `request_id`.
2) we can enable `include_trace_id` flag for their account to surface `x-redwood-trace` header in responses.
3) provide Logstash grok + mutate snippets to map header -> trace_id and send to Datadog/ELK.

danielle_se: I'll flip `include_trace_id` for acct company-xyz and temporarily raise burst limit. What's their expected QPS?

customer_xyz: Roughly 12 QPS steady, bursts to 30 for 20-40s as caching warms. Also procurement is asking about Dedicated pricing if we need predictable throughput.

mike_sales: Noted on pricing — I'll follow up with a quote. For now we'll try the flag bump.

observability_engineer: Example Logstash filter we recommend (needs structured JSON with headers field):
```
filter {
  grok { match => { \"message\" => \"%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{WORD:level} \\\\[ %{DATA:service} \\\\] %{GREEDYDATA:msg} (request_id=%{DATA:request_id})?\" } }
  mutate { add_field => { \"trace_id\" => \"%{[headers][x-redwood-trace]}\" } }
}
```
Note: Logstash can't extract HTTP headers from plain text log lines. Use Filebeat with `add_headers` or ship structured JSON logs.

danielle_se: Change pushed at 1764567950: `include_trace_id=true` for acct:company-xyz; burst limit x3 for 10m. Monitor and we'll revert if needed.

customer_xyz: Confirmed — trace_id now appears in Elastic and the 429s stopped. Dashboards look good. How to get traces into Datadog APM?

sara_se: Two options: run an OTLP collector that forwards spans to Datadog, or use our hosted span-links (we can include a `trace_url` in logs pointing to spans if they use Redwood Private/Dedicated). I'll DM you the quick steps and the pricing blurb for Dedicated.

mike_sales: :thumbsup: Great work team. I'll loop in procurement and close the POC ticket once they've validated the dashboard.
